cards.text: Grab an apron, friend, because today the crowns come off FAST. God's people are split into two kingdoms: Israel in the north and Judah in the south (1 Kings 12:16-20). In the fifteenth year of Amaziah king of Judah, Jeroboam son of Jehoash becomes king of Israel, and he reigns in Samaria forty-one years.

cards.question: Same name, different man. Jeroboam son of Nebat, the first king of the northern kingdom, led Israel into sin with golden calves (1 Kings 12:20, 28-30). What does this new King Jeroboam do about those sins?

answers.text: He doesn't turn away from them
He tears down all of them
He makes Israel repent of them

cards.text: Yep. He does evil in the sight of the LORD. And yet, PLOT TWIST: this Jeroboam wins back Israel's borders, from Lebo-hamath all the way to the Sea of the Arabah.

cards.question: The LORD had said those borders would come back, through His servant the prophet. You might know this prophet: he's the same man the LORD sent to Nineveh (Jonah 1:1-2). Who is it?

cards.text: YES, it's THAT Jonah son of Amittai (Jonah 1:1), and here we learn he's the prophet from Gath-hepher. Friend, I thought years in a junk drawer was rough, and this man spent three days and three nights inside a great fish (Jonah 1:17).
So why does the LORD do this for Israel? He sees that their suffering is very bitter, slave and free, and there's no one to help Israel.

cards.question: The LORD also had said something about Israel's future. What had He said He would not do to Israel?

answers.text: Let its enemies rule it forever

cards.question: King Jeroboam son of Jehoash also wages war and recovers two cities for Israel. Which two?

cards.text: Then Jeroboam rests with his fathers, and his son Zechariah reigns in his place.
Down south in Judah, in Jeroboam's twenty-seventh year, Azariah son of Amaziah becomes king at SIXTEEN and reigns in Jerusalem FIFTY-TWO YEARS. Friend, my batches don't last fifty-two MINUTES.

cards.question: Azariah's father Amaziah did what was right in the eyes of the LORD (2 Kings 14:3). Like his father, Azariah does what is right too.

cards.text: He sure does. But you KNOW there's a but: the high places are not taken away.

cards.question: During Azariah's reign, what do the people keep doing at the high places?

cards.text: Then the LORD afflicts King Azariah with leprosy until the day he dies, and he lives in a separate house.

cards.question: With King Azariah sick with leprosy, who takes charge of the palace and governs the people of the land?
King Azariah rests with his fathers and is buried near them in the City of David. Then his son ___ reigns in his place.

cards.text: Back up north. In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah's reign over Judah, Jeroboam's son Zechariah becomes king of Israel in Samaria. Friend, don't get too attached to this one.

cards.question: King Zechariah son of Jeroboam doesn't last long. He reigns in Samaria for just six ___.

cards.text: Six months. In that time he does evil as his fathers had done, and he doesn't turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat. Then Shallum son of Jabesh conspires against him.

cards.question: How does Shallum's conspiracy against King Zechariah end?

answers.text: He kills Zechariah in front of the people
He drives Zechariah out of Samaria
He makes Zechariah give up the throne

cards.text: Then the passage points out that a word the LORD spoke to Jehu, an earlier king of Israel, has come true. Zechariah comes from Jehu's family line.

cards.question: The LORD had told Jehu that ___ generations of his sons would sit on the throne of Israel.

cards.text: Shallum becomes king in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah's reign over Judah, and Uzziah is just another name for Azariah (2 Kings 15:7, 32). He reigns in Samaria one full month.
ONE MONTH. Friend, I've had dust sit on me in that junk drawer longer than this man sat on a throne. Then Menahem son of Gadi comes up from Tirzah to Samaria.

cards.question: Menahem son of Gadi strikes down and kills Shallum, and reigns in his place.
Then Menahem, starting from Tirzah, attacks the town of Tiphsah and everyone around it. Why does he attack Tiphsah?

answers.text: They would not open their gates
They had sided with the king of Judah

cards.text: No joke here, friend. The attack is brutal: Menahem rips open all the pregnant women.
Menahem reigns ten years in Samaria, and through his whole reign he doesn't turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat. Then Pul king of Assyria invades the land.

cards.question: When Pul king of Assyria invades, Menahem hands him a thousand talents of silver. What is Menahem after?

answers.text: His support to hold the kingdom
His help against the king of Aram

cards.question: A thousand talents is a LOT of silver. Who does Menahem collect it from?
Once Menahem pays the silver, the king of Assyria stays and takes over Samaria.

cards.text: Every wealthy man in Israel gets the same bill, fifty shekels of silver, and there's no number to call to dispute it. Then Menahem rests with his fathers, and his son Pekahiah reigns in his place.
In the fiftieth year of Azariah's reign over Judah, Pekahiah son of Menahem becomes king of Israel. He reigns two years in Samaria, and he does evil in the sight of the LORD.

cards.question: Then one of King Pekahiah's own officers conspires against him. Who is it?

cards.text: With Argob, Arieh and fifty men of Gilead, Pekah strikes down Pekahiah at the citadel of the king's palace and reigns in his place. Pekah takes the throne from PEKAHIAH, and friend, I've read that three times and I'm STILL checking who's who.

cards.question: King Pekahiah got just two years. Pekah, the officer who killed him, reigns over Israel in Samaria much longer: twenty years.

cards.text: Like the kings before him, Pekah does evil in the sight of the LORD and doesn't turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat. In his days, Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria comes and captures a whole list of towns, plus Gilead, Galilee and all the land of Naphtali.

cards.question: Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria leaves the people he captures in their own land.
Then Hoshea son of Elah leads a conspiracy against King Pekah. What does Hoshea do?

cards.text: Hoshea reigns over Israel in Pekah's place, and friend, that's the FOURTH king in this passage to get the throne by killing the king before him. Down south in Judah, back in Pekah's second year, Jotham son of Uzziah becomes king at twenty-five and reigns sixteen years in Jerusalem.
Jotham does what is right in the eyes of the LORD, just like his father Uzziah. And again, the high places stay, and the people keep sacrificing and burning incense there.

cards.question: Even with the high places still standing, King Jotham rebuilds the ___ Gate of the house of the LORD.
In King Jotham's days, Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah begin coming against Judah. Who begins to send them?

cards.text: Jotham rests with his fathers and is buried with them in the City of David, and his son Ahaz reigns in his place. Friend, that is a WHOLE lot of crowns for one batch.

findings.problem: Six of the eight choice cards are multiple choice: cards 2, 4, 7, 8, 13 and 15. With only one true-or-false card and one fill-in-the-blank card, multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the reaction "Yep.", the statement that Jeroboam does evil, and the sentence about restoring Israel's borders.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The setup asks which prophet was sent to Nineveh but cites "Jonah 1:1-2". That citation supplies the name Jonah, immediately identifying "Jonah son of Amittai" and ruling out the other two answers.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "Back up north.", the sentence introducing Zechariah's reign, and "Friend, don't get too attached to this one." It is not the walkthrough's opening card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The earlier cards only indicate that Zechariah's reign will be short. They give no basis for choosing "months" rather than "weeks" or "years", so the blank depends on luck rather than a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: "Six months.", the sentence about Zechariah's evil, and the sentence introducing Shallum's conspiracy.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker derive how many generations the LORD promised Jehu. The setup does not provide a way to reason from "four", "three" or "seven"; it only asks for an unseen number.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Four of the six choice cards depend on luck or prior Bible knowledge rather than the earlier cards: card 2 asks for the officer's name, card 4 for Pekah's exact reign length, card 6 for the captured people's fate, and card 10 for the gate's name. Only the conspiracy pattern in card 7 and the LORD's activity in card 11 offer a reasonable basis for an informed pick, so most choices in this stop are not informed guesses.

rule.text: A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The earlier cards give no clue to the gate's name. A baker cannot reason out "Upper" rather than "Horse" or "Fish" from the statement that Jotham rebuilt a gate, so this blank tests unseen wording rather than reasoned meaning.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
